[NDBG.13.7.1] **`evaluate` reads a DS expression at the current position.**
For an `evaluate` request whose `context` is
`"watch"`, `"hover"` or `"repl"`, the adapter must evaluate `expression` as a DS
expression, with the syntax of a rule `where` clause, against the bound
variables of the firing whose frame `frameId` names. Without a `frameId`, or on
the engine's thread ([NDBG.10.1.1]), the expression has no bindings. It reads
the clocks and the series as a firing at that position reads them
([LTIM.2.4.3]). This is how a watch ([LDEB.4.4]) is served. A `"repl"`
request, which a client's debug console sends for a typed line, is answered
exactly as a `"watch"`: the line is an expression and nothing else. The adapter
must answer an `evaluate` with any other `context` with an error response
naming it.

The adapter must compile the expression as it compiles a breakpoint condition
([NDBG.12.1.2]), and answer a parse or validate failure, or a program with no
source, with an error response carrying the detail. Evaluation changes nothing
in the engine ([LDEB.7.4.1]).
